evals.query: Create a Kora declarative S3 client DocumentsClient over the AWS SDK implementation with get, put, list-by-prefix and delete operations for a documents bucket.
expected_behavior: Annotates an interface with @S3.Client("s3client.documents") and lets Kora generate and register the implementation
Declares methods with @S3.Get, @S3.Put, @S3.List and @S3.Delete, using S3Object/S3ObjectList returns and S3Body for the put payload
Adds ru.tinkoff.kora.experimental:s3-client-aws plus a kora-client HTTP module and plugs AwsS3ClientModule into @KoraApp
Sets s3client.url/accessKey/secretKey/region and the required s3client.documents.bucket config key
Does not pin a version on the ru.tinkoff.kora artifacts and does not use the AWS SDK S3Client builder by hand for these operations

evals.query: I'm targeting a self-hosted MinIO server, not AWS. Which Kora S3 implementation do I use and what changes versus the AWS one?
expected_behavior: Recommends ru.tinkoff.kora.experimental:s3-client-minio with MinioS3ClientModule
Explains declarative @S3.Client interfaces are portable, so only the module on @KoraApp and a few config keys change
Notes MinIO typically needs addressStyle = "PATH" and that MinIO auto-creates an OkHttp transport
Keeps the common s3client.* config (url/accessKey/secretKey) and uses the minio-specific s3client.minio.* block for tuning
Does not mix both AwsS3ClientModule and MinioS3ClientModule into the same @KoraApp

evals.query: I need to stream a large file of unknown length up to S3 from a Kora service without buffering it all in memory.
expected_behavior: Uses S3Body.ofInputStreamUnbound(is) or S3Body.ofPublisher(pub) with no size argument for the unknown-length payload
Explains that unbound bodies automatically engage S3 multipart upload with concurrent parts
Mentions the upload.partSize tuning (default 8MiB, S3 minimum 5MiB) under s3client.aws.upload
Passes the S3Body to an @S3.Put method or the imperative S3KoraClient
Does not read the whole stream into a byte[] with S3Body.ofBytes for a large unknown-length file

evals.query: On my Kora @S3.Client I want per-tenant object keys like docs/{tenantId}/{docId}.pdf for get, put and delete.
expected_behavior: Uses templated keys such as @S3.Put("docs/{tenantId}/{docId}.pdf") with {argName} placeholders
Ensures every method argument appears in the template with no extra unused args
Interpolates arguments via toString(), so UUID/String args substitute directly
Notes that multi-key operations taking List<String> cannot use a key template
Does not concatenate the bucket name into the key or hand-build the key inside the interface method

evals.query: I only need to check an object exists and read its size/content-type in Kora S3, not download the body. What's the efficient way?
expected_behavior: Declares an @S3.Get method returning S3ObjectMeta so Kora issues a HEAD request with no body transfer
For listings, uses S3ObjectMetaList / an @S3.List method returning meta to skip body fetching
Explains S3ObjectMeta is faster because no object data is transferred
Notes deletes are best-effort so a meta get is the way to assert existence
Does not fetch a full S3Object body just to read metadata

evals.query: The declarative annotations don't cover what I need in Kora S3 - I want dynamic buckets and presigned URLs. What do I inject?
expected_behavior: Injects the portable S3KoraClient or S3KoraAsyncClient by constructor for imperative operations
Explains the imperative client covers cases declarative @S3.* annotations don't (dynamic buckets, batch delete reporting, presigned URLs, ACL, versioning)
Mentions the native clients (S3Client/S3AsyncClient for AWS, MinioClient for MinIO) are also injectable for implementation-specific features
Keeps a single S3 module on @KoraApp and uses constructor injection
Does not instantiate the AWS or MinIO SDK client manually outside the Kora graph
